test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 17 Nov, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question:
Which of the following statements is correct?

a) India is the only country in the world that has both tigers and lions.

b) The natural habitat of the Indian lion is the Gir forest in Gujarat. Tigers are found in the forests of Madhya Pradesh, the Sundarbans of West Bengal and the Himalayan region.

options.text: Both a and b are incorrect.
Both a and b are correct.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both a and b are correct.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **India is the only country in the world** that has both tigers and lions in the wild.
 
• The natural habitat of the Indian lion is the **Gir Forest in Gujarat**, which is the only place in the world where Asiatic lions are found.
 
• **Tigers in India** are distributed across various regions, including the forests of Madhya Pradesh, the Sundarbans of West Bengal, and parts of the Himalayan region.
 
• India is home to **significant populations of these big cats** and has numerous conservation programs in place to protect them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gir Forest National Park**

 
 
• Located in Gujarat, India, it is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion (Panthera leo persica).
 
• It was established in 1965 and covers a total area of approximately 1,412 km².
 
• The park is also home to a diverse range of wildlife including leopards, antelopes, and a variety of bird species.
 
• Conservation efforts have been successful in increasing the population of Asiatic lions.
 
 
 
• **Tiger Conservation in India**
 
 
• India is home to around 70% of the world's tiger population.
 
• The major habitats include the forests of Madhya Pradesh, the Sundarbans in West Bengal, and parts of the Western Ghats and the Himalayan region.
 
• India has established numerous tiger reserves under the Project Tiger initiative launched in 1973 to protect and increase the tiger population.
 
• Some well-known tiger reserves are the Kanha and Bandhavgarh reserves in Madhya Pradesh, and the Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Challenges**
 
 
• Both tigers and lions face threats from habitat loss, poaching, and human-wildlife conflict.
